hook: The philosopher of Königsberg who asked what we can know and how we should act.

pages.x: Immanuel Kant was born in 1724 in Königsberg, in Prussia, now Kaliningrad in Russia, the son of a harness maker. In his whole life he never travelled more than about 100 km from his city.
He kept such a strict routine that neighbours were said to set their clocks by his afternoon walk. He missed it, the story goes, only when he was lost in reading Rousseau's Emile.

pages.t: How the Sun and planets formed
pages.x: In 1755 he suggested that the solar system formed from a spinning cloud of gas and dust, and that faint smudges in the sky were whole galaxies of stars.
pages.fx: Scientists still explain the birth of the Sun and planets in much this way, and he was right about the galaxies.

pages.x: At 57 he published the Critique of Pure Reason, asking what we can know. The mind, he argued, is not a blank slate: it shapes experience itself, with space, time and cause built in. It is one of the most important, and hardest, books in philosophy.
In morals, he said, act only by rules you could want everyone to follow, and treat people always as ends in themselves, never just as tools. This idea of human dignity underlies human rights today.
pages.img: Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals

pages.x: In 1795 he proposed a league of free nations to end war for ever, an idea that inspired the League of Nations and the United Nations.
Kant is one of the greatest philosophers of all time. His tomb bears his famous words: "The starry heavens above me and the moral law within me."
pts: Wrote the Critique of Pure Reason
Taught that people must be treated as ends, never only as means
Imagined a league of nations for lasting peace
